Local news from the three cities

Short summaries of other outlets’ reporting, newest first. Each links to the original.

Residents raise data center concerns at New Kensington council

New to you · About Sept. 2026 · New Kensington

Voice of Westmoreland members asked about data center talks; Mayor Tom Guzzo said the city has none and signed no NDAs, and promised public forums if any arise.

Source: TribLive community news

Public open house on PSU New Kensington campus future

New to you · Aug. 2026 · New Kensington

An Aug. 11 open house in the campus auditorium sought input; officials stress the property is not sold and no developer is chosen.

Source: Westmoreland County

PRT proposes new New Kensington–Highlands Mall bus route

New to you · Aug. 2026 · New Kensington

PRT's final Bus Line Redesign proposal adds 7-day N3 service linking New Kensington, Arnold, Tarentum, Brackenridge and Natrona Heights; comments due Sept. 30.

Source: Pittsburgh Regional Transit

Community visioning launches for Penn State New Kensington site

New to you · June 2026 · New Kensington

The Economic Growth Connection opened a survey (June 23) and pop-up meetings at Fridays on Fifth to gather ideas for reusing the campus.

Source: Westmoreland County

Lower Burrell officials press for more new businesses

New to you · May 2026 · Lower Burrell

Mayor Chris Fabry cited seven new or imminent businesses including Gio's Restaurant, MW Mechanical and Tractor Supply.

Source: TribLive community news

Fridays on Fifth returns with October date added

New to you · April 2026

The downtown street festival runs the fourth Friday April-October 2026.

Source: Valley News Dispatch (TribLive)

Penn State realigns Digital Foundry and LaunchBox under research office

New to you · March 2026 · New Kensington

The New Kensington innovation spaces moved under the Office of the Senior VP for Research to secure long-term support.

Source: psu.edu

Arnold police get body cameras

New to you · About March 2026 · Arnold

Mayor Shannon Santucci secured body-worn cameras; the $13,350 cost was split with DA Nicole Ziccarelli's office.

Source: TribLive community news

Burrell sells Stewart School site for housing

New to you · Feb. 2026

The board approved a $1 sale of the 8.44-acre Stewart property to developer David Ziccarelli for 46 duplex-style condos, expected to generate about a mill of taxes.

Source: TribLive community news

Horizon Market ends downtown New Kensington food desert

New to you · Dec. 2025 · New Kensington

A small-scale grocery opened Dec. 10 at 912 Seventh St. in the former Molnor Antiques building.

Source: WPXI

Lower Burrell Tractor Supply pushed to spring

New to you · Dec. 2025 · Lower Burrell

The store at 108 Greensburg Road, originally slated for November 2025, planned a late-March soft opening and mid-April grand opening.

Source: TribLive community news

New Kensington fire companies consolidate; Parnassus station to close

New to you · Sept. 2025 · New Kensington

Council recognized the merger of three volunteer companies into Citizens Volunteer Fire Company No. 1; the Parnassus station on Freeport Street is recommended for sale.

Source: TribLive community news

Arnold and New Kensington American Legion posts merge

New to you · Sept. 2025 · Arnold

Declining membership led Arnold Post 684 and New Kensington Post 347 to form the Ar-Ken American Legion Post 347.

Source: Valley News Dispatch (TribLive)

Earlier: 2025 (7)

Burrell's Stewart Elementary closes; grades reconfigured

New to you · About Aug. 2025

Starting 2025-26, Bon Air serves K-4 and Huston houses grades 5-8 after the board's 9-0 vote to close the nearly century-old Stewart Elementary.

Source: Valley News Dispatch (TribLive)

$7M PA SITES grant for New Kensington Advanced Manufacturing Park

New to you · May 2025 · New Kensington

Gov. Shapiro awarded RIDC $6.98M to rehab ~130,000 sq ft in Buildings 37 and 38 of the former Alcoa works.

Source: WPXI

Penn State trustees vote to close Penn State New Kensington

New to you · May 2025 · New Kensington

Trustees voted 25-8 on May 22 to close seven Commonwealth campuses, including New Kensington, after the spring 2027 semester.

Source: radio.wpsu.org

Starbucks opens at Riverview Plaza

New to you · Feb. 2025

Drive-thru Starbucks opened Feb. 25 on Tarentum Bridge Road, following Harbor Freight's January opening at the former Kmart site; Wingstop also coming.

Source: TribLive community news

Westmoreland Transit updates Route 14

New to you · Feb. 2025 · Lower Burrell

Route 14 serving Lower Burrell, New Kensington, Arnold and Pittsburgh Mills got a revised schedule effective February 2025.

Source: westmorelandtransit.com

Re:Build launches Re:Build Battery Solutions in New Kensington

New to you · Jan. 2025 · New Kensington

The contract manufacturer anchoring the former Alcoa site launched a battery engineering/manufacturing company based at its 175,000 sq ft New Kensington plant.

Source: rebuildmanufacturing.com

New Kensington-Arnold board limits possible tax increase

New to you · Jan. 2025 · New Kensington

The school board voted unanimously not to exceed its state index for 2025-26; the preliminary budget proposed a 3-mill increase.

Source: Valley News Dispatch (TribLive)
